Definition: from G4509; to soil, i.e. (intransitively) to become dirty (morally):--be filthy.
BiblicalUsage: When the text says rhypóō, it means to soil, that is (intransitively) to become dirty (morally). It stands in Revelation 22:11, where the King James Version reads, "…be unjust still: and he which is filthy…" — but the SBL text there reads a different verb, ῥυπαρεύω.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the warning stands even so: the filthy are left to their filth, and the holy to their holiness.
